purpose: Cross-check every registered regime label with a standalone Decimal oracle

lifecycle.idea: Challenge the classifier with a second implementation rather than another self-test
lifecycle.hypothesis: A standalone Decimal oracle reproduces every registered label within a fixed tolerance
lifecycle.critique: Both implementations still share one specification and constructed inputs
lifecycle.decision: Accept implementation equivalence; reject market-validity inference
lifecycle.lesson: Independent arithmetic catches implementation drift but cannot validate the model itself

limitations: Both implementations share the same regime contract
No manual golden labels or external engine
No historical accuracy, calibration, execution or PnL evidence
verification: 28 labels and 196 fields cross-checked with zero mismatches
tampered class and numeric metric produce BLOCKED
lessons: A second numeric representation reduces common implementation risk
Mismatch reports must be retained rather than converted into exceptions
Specification and market validity need separate challenges
